newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar settles firmer but well off highs.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar settles firmer but well off highs.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures closed firmer but off the day's highs after early buying failed to attract follow-through, trading sources said.

The trade carried the benchmark October contract through stops around 11.34 cents and to its contract high of 11.40 cents, where trade selling knocked October back towards the middle of the day's range.
Dealers also noted brisk buying in March, which lifted the second-position contract to a new, life-of-contract high of 11.40 cents.
The October contract closed 0.05 cent firmer at 11.24 cents per lb, traded 11.40 to 11.21 cents. The rest of the board settled 0.06 to 0.10 cent higher.
Nearby resistance in October was pegged at its lifetime high of 11.40 cents, followed by 11.50 cents.

Trading sources expect rangebound and thin dealings ahead of the Independence Day holiday on Friday. In the near term, swelling open interest in the October contract could prompt some liquidation, they said.
"Open interest is outrageously high. We may be getting a little top-heavy," a sugar broker said.
As of Monday, open interest in the spot month climbed to 94,790 lots, up 2,000 lots from the previous session.
"A lot of people rolled sugar from July to October, so there is a lot around for October delivery, the broker said. "No one is sure what will happen between now and October 1."
Some market sources said a lack of physical offtake will begin to weigh on the market, while others said CSCE world sugar futures will maintain their recent 10.00 to 12.00 cent trading range.

"The difference between the past six months and the semester ahead is that the market is apt to spend more time testing the upper boundaries of the 10-12 cent range rather than drifting towards the lower end of the band," Merrill Lynch said in a global outlook.
An estimated 21,896 lots changed hands on the day, compared with Monday's official 15,781 lots.
